title: Hiring Loop
description:
You applied. 4,000 other people applied. Get one job candidate through eight interview rounds, from resume screening to the in-person on-site, in a rage platformer where the floor drops, the recruiter ghosts you, the requirements pivot mid-jump, and every death is a rejection email.
Each round is worse than the last. Made the day I got rejected from five roles.
controls: Left/Right or A/D move, Space/W/Up jump (hold for higher), R restart round, P or Esc pause, M mute. On phones: on-screen left/right pad, JUMP, pause and restart buttons.

provenance.prompt: New game. The core concept is the same, but instead of a ghost it's a job candidate's journey through a very aggressive job market. I just got rejected from 5 roles today and I want to show how frustrating that is. The candidate has to pass every obstacle to get to work at the company; make it really hard to pass. Each level is an interview step and it gets incrementally worse: 1 screening, 2 recruiter, 3 assessment, 4 live coding, 5 system design, 6 manager screening, 7 CEO/CTO screening, 8 in-person interview (a completely new environment, maybe outdoors). Same controls and responsiveness. Create a demo video.
provenance.notes: Kept Haunt Loop's engine untouched: physics constants, controls, touch layout, the trap system and the level verifier. Changed: the ghost is now a job candidate in a suit; six levels became eight interview rounds; deaths are rejections with rejection-email taunts; rounds 1-7 are a late-night office, round 8 (on-site) is a new outdoor scene with grass, traffic cones and the HQ on the horizon. New trap types: chase (a deadline wall that slides in), reverse (a pivot that flips your controls), plus traps that only arm after 1 or 2 deaths in a round. Every round's winning route was found by a beam search over the game's own sim and is checked by tools/verify-levels.mjs, so each round is hard but proven beatable. Demo, thumbnail and screenshots were recorded from ?autopilot, which replays those verified inputs frame by frame; no human play is shown.
